albums.blurb: Detroit guitarist Kenny Burrell was one of the house players of Blue Note's golden era, and Midnight Blue is his signature statement: a stripped-down, piano-less session cut in a single January 1963 date at Van Gelder Studio, with Stanley Turrentine on tenor saxophone, Major Holley on bass, Bill English on drums, and Ray Barretto on conga. The set is built almost entirely from Burrell's own simmering minor-key blues originals — the opener "Chitlins con Carne" was later covered by Stevie Ray Vaughan — and it stays instrumental from end to end.
albums.reception: AllMusic's Scott Yanow called it one of Burrell's best-known sessions for the Blue Note label, and Jazz Improv magazine placed it among its top five recommended Burrell recordings, pointing to it as the place to hear "the Blue Note sound."

albums.blurb: Because the Internet is Donald Glover's second studio album as Childish Gambino, released on Glassnote in December 2013 alongside a companion screenplay meant to be read while the record plays. It marks the pivot point in his discography: the punchline-dense rapping of Camp gives way to woozy production, sung hooks, and the funk and soul instincts that would fully take over on "Awaken, My Love!" three years later. It produced the singles "3005," "Sweatpants," and "Telegraph Ave."
albums.reception: The album debuted at number seven on the Billboard 200, earned a Grammy nomination for Best Rap Album in 2015, and was certified gold by the RIAA in 2016.

albums.blurb: Olivia Dean is an east London singer and BRIT School graduate whose warm, retro-leaning soul-pop draws on classic Motown craft as much as contemporary UK R&B. Messy, released on EMI in June 2023 and led by the single "Dive," is her debut studio album after a run of EPs, and it is the record that established her before the 2025 follow-up The Art of Loving.
albums.reception: Messy debuted at number four on the UK Albums Chart, was shortlisted for the 2023 Mercury Prize, and has been certified gold by the BPI.
